title: HelioSpark onboarding handoff & integration plan
summary: Kickoff/hand-off meeting between Redwood CSM/AE/SE and HelioSpark platform team to align on VPC connectivity, SSO, KMS, pilot workload shapes, and pilot timeline. Agreed on a 2-week smoke test then a 6-week pilot; Redwood to share runbook, network checklist, and a small benchmark template. Customer requested SOC2 + network diagrams and an on-prem integration note. Several follow-ups assigned.
topics: VPC peering & connectivity options (Direct Connect vs VPN)
SAML/SCIM SSO integration and RBAC mapping
action_items: Priya Shah (Redwood): Send onboarding runbook, network checklist, and sample benchmark spreadsheet - due 2026-04-07
Marco Alvarez (Redwood SE): Prepare a short latency/cost micro-benchmark on customer-like workload (2 prompts) and share results - due 2026-04-09
Dana Liu (HelioSpark): Share service account IP ranges and primary VPC CIDR + firewall contacts - due 2026-04-06
Lena Ortiz (HelioSpark SecOps): Confirm KMS vendor preferences and compliance questions to Redwood security - due 2026-04-10
next_steps: Schedule smoke test window: target 2026-04-09 to 2026-04-10
Redwood to upload SOC2 summary + network diagram to shared drive by 2026-04-06
Follow-up technical deep dive for VPC peering on 2026-04-08 (SE-led)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-04
Start time: 13:30 PDT
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim, Priya Shah, Marco Alvarez (Redwood) — Dana Liu, Omar Reyes, Lena Ortiz, Markus Hwang (HelioSpark)

Auto-summary: handoff and integration planning, doc share commitments, smoke test schedule

[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're calling this the onboarding handoff, I'll quickly run through agenda. Priya and Marco are here from CS and SE. Dana, do you want to kick off with a quick intro to the team and what success looks like?

[00:32] Dana Liu: Sure, thanks Alex. Hi all — Dana here, head of ML Ops at HelioSpark. We're building a virtual assistant for field techs and a diagnostics pipeline that will call the model for routing suggestions. Success for us is stable sub-200ms p95 generator for the majority of calls and ability to keep data in our VPC. Timeline is Q2 pilot then production Q3, but roll is somewhat flexible.

[01:05] Omar Reyes: Hi I'm Omar — platform. We'll own the network and infra side, doing VPC peering and firewall work. Main constraint is we have strict egress rules and we prefer private deployment or dedicated underscores — sorry — dedicated pool, we want data isolated.

[01:28] Alex Kim: Great context. Marco, high-level from a runtime perspective?

[01:35] Marco Alvarez: Yeah hi all. From Redwood side we support three modes — hosted, dedicated, private VPC. For your isolation ask, Private deployment with customer-managed VPC is common. We do recommend starting with dedicated to get consistent throughput, then move to private if you need network control. For the p95 latency goal — we usually look at prompt length distributions and kv cache patterns; if you can share a sample of typical prompt sizes we'll size the pool.

[02:12] Lena Ortiz: Quick security question, sorry, is the KV cache ever stored outside customer keys? We need to know about encryption at rest and KMS or HSM integration.

[02:24] Marco Alvarez: Good point. By default ephemeral KV caches are in memory on the serving nodes; for private deployments you can leverage your KMS for root keys — Redwood supports customer KMS in our private control plane. I'll add an architecture note after the call.

[02:48] Markus Hwang: How about audit logs and retention? We have 7-year retention requirements for some telemetry.

[02:55] Priya Shah: We have an enterprise observability add-on that can push logs to your S3 with configurable retention; we also provide audit logs in the control plane. I'll share the SOC2 summary and the audit export docs.

[03:12] Dana Liu: That would be great. Also want to understand the network topologies: direct connect vs ipsec vpn — which is more reliable?

[03:24] Alex Kim: In our experience Direct Connect (or cloud provider equivalent) is lower latency and more consistent, but more setup time and cost. VPN is quicker to set up for a pilot. We'll put both options in the runbook and mark pros/cons.

[04:00] [Speaker 1]: (mumble) can you also outline the failover plan if the dedicated pool degrades?

[04:10] Marco Alvarez: Yep — we have fallback policies that route to compatible model variants in other regions or hosted endpoints; we can set automatic fallback with throttling and signals so the app stays online. We'll propose an A/B canary during rollout.

[04:45] Omar Reyes: For the smoke test, what are you expecting us to provide? Just a few example prompts and network settings?

[04:55] Priya Shah: Exactly. We'll need prompt samples, preferred SSO provider info for SCIM/SAML, and a list of IPs/service accounts. Also a basic request volume estimate — concurrent RPS and average tokens per request.

[05:15] Dana Liu: For RPS, initial is light — maybe 15 concurrent calls with a burst to 80 for 30s; tokens per request avg 120, but sometimes up to 900 for long diagnostics.

[05:35] Marco Alvarez: That long tail matters. For up to 900 tokens we'll recommend slightly different kernel and batching settings; I'll include quantization guidance in the doc.

[06:00] Lena Ortiz: On SSO, we are using Okta and want SCIM provisioning for service accounts and RBAC mapping to our groups. Any gotchas?

[06:12] Marco Alvarez: Okta + SCIM is supported. We'll need to map your Okta groups to Redwood roles; for the private control plane customers can require SAML SSO and enforce SSO-only logins. Priya will coordinate the SCIM provisioning steps.

[06:40] [00:07:00] Alex Kim: Switching gears to pilot success criteria — Dana, you mentioned p95, anything else?

[06:50] Dana Liu: We'll measure latency percentiles, model correctness on a checklist of 50 prompts, and cost per 1k tokens as a soft metric. If latency or correctness regresses during pilot, we'll pause rollout.

[07:12] Priya Shah: Great — we'll include an eval harness template so you can run automated checks against a reference prompt set. We also recommend instrumenting the SDK side for token-level telemetry.

[07:30] Markus Hwang: On the legal/compliance side — do you have a data processing addendum? Also need to know about data residency — we prefer US-EAST region for now.

[07:42] Priya Shah: Yes we have DPAs and region pinning for Dedicated/Private deployments. I'll attach the legal pack and a pinned region agreement.

[08:00] Omar Reyes: For the network, I can share our CIDRs right after this call. Two small asks: 1) a plain network diagram we can paste into our change control requests, 2) a short runbook for firewall rules.

[08:15] Alex Kim: We'll provide both. Priya will drop a runbook + diagram.

[08:30] [00:10:00] Marco Alvarez: Quick technical note — if you plan to use the on-prem option, latency to edge devices may improve but operational overhead increases; given your early stage pilot we usually recommend dedicated or private cloud deployment. We can simulate on-prem behavior in a benchmark though.

[09:05] Dana Liu: Does Redwood support encrypting cache with HSM-backed KMS? We may need FIPS compliance in future.

[09:18] Marco Alvarez: We support customer-managed KMS and can integrate with HSM-backed providers; the FIPS path may require additional validation steps, which we'll document.

[09:45] Lena Ortiz: Can you explain the rollout cadence? We want a canary then gradual traffic ramp.

[09:53] Priya Shah: Typical rollout is canary (10% traffic), monitor for two days, then 50%, then full. We provide tracing hooks and can roll back automatically if error rates increase.

[10:20] [00:15:00] Alex Kim: Let's lock in dates — we're proposing a short smoke test on 2026-04-09, then a 6-week pilot starting 2026-04-13 if smoke test looks good. Does that match your internal planning?

[10:35] Dana Liu: That works for us — ops team will schedule maintenance windows.

[10:45] Omar Reyes: One more practical: do you need us to open outbound egress to a specific set of IPs, or do you support VPC peering so no egress changes?

[10:58] Marco Alvarez: We support both. For quick pilots VPN with opening a few IP(s) is fastest; for production we prefer VPC peering or PrivateLink equivalents. We'll send the IP ranges in the network checklist.

[11:20] [00:20:00] [Speaker 2]: (overlap) any pricing expectations for the pilot — ballpark?

[11:30] Alex Kim: We'll share a pilot pricing estimate — typical pilots run as usage plus a small reserved block for baseline. For the 6-week pilot we'll send a tailored estimate based on your RPS and token profiles.

[11:55] Dana Liu: Please include both hosted and dedicated pricing just so we can compare.

[12:05] Priya Shah: We'll include both and a TCO note showing cost per 1k tokens under typical batching and quantization settings.

[12:30] Marco Alvarez: Back to technical, I'll need a small sample of requests — two prompts: one short and one long — to run micro-benchmarks. That will help with kernel selection and memory footprint estimates.

[12:48] Dana Liu: We'll send that by EOD tomorrow.

[13:02] [00:30:00] Alex Kim: Ok let's summarize action items and next steps — Priya to send runbook and legal pack; Marco to run micro-benchmarks; Dana to share CIDRs and sample prompts. Priya, can you confirm timeline?

[13:20] Priya Shah: Yes, runbook + SOC2 + network diagram by 2026-04-06, benchmark results 2026-04-09, smoke test 2026-04-09 to 2026-04-10 and full pilot start 2026-04-13.

[13:40] Lena Ortiz: One last question — is there any offline documentation about model quantization tradeoffs?

[13:48] Marco Alvarez: Yes, I'll attach a short note with recommended quantization profiles and expected latency/cost impact. It's usually a small doc.

[14:05] Markus Hwang: If everything looks good after the smoke test, we'll need a runbook handoff to our SREs. Who will be the primary contact?

[14:12] Priya Shah: I'll be primary CSM contact; Marco is technical lead. Alex will be escalation point.

[14:30] [00:40:00] Alex Kim: Thanks everyone. Any blockers we didn't capture?

[14:36] Dana Liu: Not at the moment — we just need the documents and the quick benchmarks.

[14:45] Alex Kim: Great — we'll send the artifacts and calendar invites for the smoke test and the VPC deep dive. Thanks all.

[15:00] Omar Reyes: Thanks — appreciate it.

[15:10] [00:56:30] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional overlap and minor mis-heard words. Names mostly accurate but may be slightly off in places.
